context:
Goal: the red-main check never says green while main is red, and never blocks merges while main is green.
Problem (rule): Main now skips its full test run after a green PR run of the same code (your ruling own-769). A skipped run proves nothing, so the check must look back to a run that really ran the tests. The first way I built to do that can be fooled: a docs-only PR shows green even though its tests were skipped, so it could wrongly clear a red main.
Based on (read): lane merge-flow-after-anthropic's reads on PR #3297, via the coordinator 18:08 CST; unchecked by triage. How far back main's newest test-running run sits is unmeasured.
Departs from: the 16:06 CST wording on step red-gate-reads-suite-run and the cover in main's red-main check — a and b drop the cover; your ruling own-769 (the skip itself) stays.
Meanwhile: PR #3297 waits.

options.gain: A red main can never read green by mistake; no extra reads.
options.label: Judge only runs that ran the tests
options.lose: A docs-only fix of a red main stays red until a code push goes green, or someone uses --base-red-ok.

options.gain: The judged run is never stale.
options.label: Same as a, plus a full test run on main when the judged run is old
options.lose: An extra full run on main each time, so more CI minutes and Mac spend.

options.gain: You pick on real numbers: how far back main's newest test-running run sits.
options.label: Measure first, then choose between a and b (triage recommends)
options.lose: PR #3297 waits until the measure is read.
